lawyer:
Amir Hossain with Farzana Hoque, Advocates ------ For the Appellants
Abdul Kuddus Mia, Advocate ------ For the Respondents.
parties:
Mayurer Nessa and others ------ Appellants
vs
Julekha Khatoon and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: This appeal by the contesting defendant Nos. 1 and 8 is against judgment and decree dated 26.9.1972 passed by the Addl. District Judge, Comilla in Title Appeal No. 95 of 1967 affirming the judgment and decree dated 18.3.1967 passed by Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Comilia in Title Suit No. 69 of 1965. 2. Respondent Nos. 1-14 as plaintiffs filed the aforesaid suit of partition of the suit property claiming plaintiffs’ No. 1-13 as heirs of one of the recorded tenant Rahmat Ali whose name was recorded in the CS Khatian Ext. 2 as owner of 0.08 annas share of the jote. According to the plaintiffs, plaintiff No. 14 is the purchaser from the plaintiff No. 2. The plaintiffs claimed that other recorded tenant of the suit kharian was Alabuddin, predecessor-in-interest of defendant Nos. 1-19, and defendant Nos. 20-23 are purchasers from the said defendants. Plaintiffs claimed partition On the ground that there was no partition by metes and bounds and taking advantage of wrong entry regarding possession in the CS khatian the defendants had been disturbing their possession. On such allegations plaintiff filed the suit on 27.1.63. 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 8 contested the suit by filing a joint written statement denying material allegations and stating that the suit property originally belonged to their predecessor Alabuddin who took lease of the same from the landlord on tile basis of kabuliyat and patta from the landlord Gouri Pria Debi at an annual jama of Taka 16.00 and as the taluk of Gouripria Debi was purchased by Nabin Chandra Chakraborty said Alabuddin executed a kabuliyat in favour of the purchaser landlord who also executed a paua in his favour on 24th Kartick, 1310 BS Ext. 'A'. Since then Alabuddin was in possession of the entire suit property. Further case of the defendants was that the said Alabuddin had a brother named Sona Guzi who married mother of plaintiffs predecessor Rahmat Ali who came to the house of Sona Gazi and after the death of Sonagazi and his 2nd wife out of compassion Alabuddin allowed Rahmat Ali to possess the Suit plot Nos.160, 224 and 226. Taking advantage of old age and ignorance of Alabuddin the said Rahmat Ali during the CS operation wrongly recorded 0.08 annas share of the suit land in the suit khatian though he had no title in the suit property. Further case of the contesting defendants is that Yusuf Ali and Jinnat Ali, two sons of Alabuddin while in title and possession of the suit land executed a confirmatory kabuliyat in favour of landlord, Nabin Chakraborty on 4th Agrahayan 1331 BS and got a paua on the same date from the said landlord Ext. A(1) and since then they are in possession of the entire suit land except those three suit plots on payment of rents from before CS khatian in the name of Alabuddin and his heirs vide Ext. 'B' series. Their further case is that sons of Rahmat Ali relinquished possession of plot Nos. 224 and 226 in favour of Ishab Ali and Jinnat Ali after taking settlement of some land from them by a kabuliyat dated 3rd Chaitra, 1330 BS Ext. C. Their further case is that Alabuddin and after his death his heirs paid rent of the suit property to the landlord. 4. On consideration of the evidence on record trial Court found that Rahmat Ali had 8 annas share in the suit land and decreed the suit for partition of 8 annas share in favour of the plaintiff in preliminary form of the entire suit property excepting plot No. 238. Court of appeal below affirmed the aforesaid finding of the trial Court. 5. Mr. Amir Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants, submitted that both the Courts below failed to hold that the presumption of correctness of the entry in the CS khatian Ext. 2 recording 8 annas share in favour of plaintiffs' predecessor Rahmat Ali was rebutted by the paua Ext. 'A' registered on 16.11.1903 long before the preparation of CS khatian Ext. 2 and the payment of rents alone by Alabuddin. 6. It appears that trial Court found that Alabuddin had 8 annas share and Rahmat Ali had 8 annas share in the suit tenancy although the original patta stood in the name of Alabuddin alone and that Rahmat Ali was in possession of about half of the tenancy. On the other hand Court of appeal below found that Alabuddin took lease on his own behalf and on behalf of his nephew Rahmat Ali and the plaintiffs have possession in the suit land. But none, of the Courts below found in which suit plots plaintiffs have exclusive or joint possession. It is not denied that only plot Nos. 160, 224 and 226 having an area of 50 acres were recorded in exclusive possession of plaintiffs' predecessor Rahmat Ali in the CS khatian Ext. 2 and other 10 plots except homestead plot No. 224 were recorded in exclusive possession of defendants predeceassor Alabuddin in the said khatian. Though the plaintiffs stated in para 7 of the plaint that Alabuddin and Rahmat Ali possessed the suit land in equal share and entry regarding exclusive possession in the CS khatian was wrong they did not state in which other plots they had possession. Plaintiffs adduced evidence to the effect that before compromise they possessed 7/8 plots and after compromise they possess 5 plots but none of the PWs could say in which plots plaintiffs possessed before compromise. Trial Court without considering the presumption of entry regarding possession in the CS khatian, failure of the PWs to state the plot numbers in which plaintiffs had possession and reliability of the PWs erroneously opined that plaintiffs previously possessed 7/8 plots. If the entry in the CS khatian Ext. 2 regarding share of plaintiffs' predecessor Rahmat Ali and defendants' predecessor Alabuddin is found to be correct the entry regarding exclusive possession of the said two persons cannot be found to be incorrect. As a matter of fact none of the Courts below specifically found the said entry regarding exclusive possession in the said CS khatian to be wrong or incorrect. I do not find any illegality in the finding of the Courts below regarding share of the parties in the suit property as recorded in the CS khatian inasmuch as both the Courts below considered the patta Ext. A and rent receipts Ext. B series in the name of Alabuddin along with other evidence on record for arriving at the said finding. But I fail to agree with the finding of the Courts below regarding possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land as the same suffers from non-consideration of material evidence on record and presumption arising from entry in the CS Khatian. 7. CS khatian Ext. 2 clearly shows that except homestead plot No. 234 all other plots were recorded in exclusive possession of the said Alabuddin and Rahmat Ali respectively. From the same it is clear that long before the CS operation they possessed the suit plots except plot No. 234 separately and exclusively and homestead plot No. 234 was only in their ejmali possession. From their above conduct it can easily be inferred that there was amicable partition between them in respect of those plots recorded in their respective exclusive possession. When CS khatian records a jote in the name of several persons having distinct share therein but the lands are recorded in exclusive possession of the respective co-sharers then there remains nothing to partition the lands unless the entry regarding exclusive possession is found to be wrong and incorrect. Had the entry regarding exclusive possession in the CS khatian been wrong Rahmat Ali or his heirs would not have remained silent for about fifty years from the date of final publication of the CS khatian. Such exclusive possession of a party in the land for a long period should not be easily disturbed on the flimsy allegation of a co-sharer in the jote unless he can prove by evidence that presumption of correctness of such entry is erroneous. 8. It appears from judgment of the trial Court that the suit was decreed on compromise between the plaintiffs and defendant Nos. 2, 3 and 12-17 on 4.3.61 and ex parte against the rest and subsequently appellants filed a Miscellaneous Case and got the decree set aside on 27.3.65 and thereafter they contested the suit and lost upto the Court of appeal below. The compromising defendants being male descendants of Alabuddin at the earliest opportunity compromised the suit with the plaintiffs by giving up their possession in same plots in favour of the plaintiffs in consideration of their relinquishing some share in the suit property in favour of defendants to avoid litigation and protect their possession in other plots in spite of their exclusive possession in 10 plots and even after setting aside of the ex parte decree they neither contested the suit nor disowned the compromise. Plaintiff No. 1 Kala Mia deposing as PW 1 stated that according to the terms of that compromise plaintiffs gave up possession of some lands and they are in possession of the remaining land. PW 2 also supported PW 1 as to plaintiffs' possession of 1.52 acres of land in plot Nos. 160, 161, 320, 367 and 400 in terms of compromise. It appears from joint petition of compromise dated 4.3.64 filed by the plaintiffs and aforesaid defendant Nos. 2, 3, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 that the plaintiffs were given in possession in the aforesaid five plots having an area of 1.52 acres and they were allowed decree in 76/23 share of the suit property and they abandoned their claim in the rest of the suit property in favour of compromising defendants. Since none of the compromising parties abandoned the said compromise it is difficult to understand why the Courts below did not consider the same while passing the impugned judgment and decree. 9. Order 23 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that at any time after institution of the suit plaintiffs may as against all or any of the defendants withdraw his suit or abandon any part of his claim. Plaintiffs having abandoned their claim in respect of part of the suit property in the said petition of compromise effected at the intervention of relations and well-wishers of the parties and village matbars they cannot get a decree as claimed in the plaint in respect of 8 annas share of the suit property. None of the village Matbars came to support plaintiffs' claim of possession in 7/8 plots before the said compromise. From the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 it transpires that the said compromise was acted upon between compromising parties. Had the contesting defendants’ appellants been successful in dislodging the claim of the plaintiffs and establishing their claim that defendants were thel6 annas owners of the suit property then the compromise could not be considered and given effect to. But the defendant appellants having failed to establish that their predecessor Alabuddin was 16 annas owner of the suit property, male decendants of Alabuddin who are residents of the suit village could not be deprived of the benefit of the compromise acted upon between the compromising parties for the mere fancy and folly of non-resident female decendants of Alabuddin who never actually possessed any part of the suit property. 10. Partition is an equitable relief. Compromising defendants having given up their possession in favour of the plaintiffs in some of the suit plots in consideration of plaintiffs' relinquishing some portion of their share in the suit property in favour of the defendants and the same having been acted upon the plaintiffs are estopped from giving a go by to the same to the prejudice of the said defendants. 11. In the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case I find that decision of the Courts below is contrary to law in not giving effect to the compromise effected between the plaintiffs and non-contesting defendants though acted upon by those parties. 12. In view of the above I find substance in this appeal not on the ground as taken by the appellants but on the ground that the plaintiffs are estopped from claiming 8 annas share giving a go by to the compromise acted upon between the compromising parties. In the result, the appeal is allowed in part without cost and the judgments and decrees of the Courts below are modified and the suit is decreed in part in preliminary form in terms of compromise petition dated 4.3.1964. End.
